stem:
Statements:
All pens are books.
All books are bags.
Conclusions:
I. All pens are bags.
II. Some bags are pens.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow from the statements?
explanation: Pens are inside books and books are inside bags, so all pens are bags — I follows. Converting 'All pens are bags' gives 'Some bags are pens' — II follows.
shortcut: All A are B converts to Some B are A

stem:
Statements:
Some cats are dogs.
No dog is a rat.
Conclusions:
I. Some cats are not rats.
II. No cat is a rat.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow from the statements?
explanation: The cats that are dogs cannot be rats, so some cats are definitely not rats — I follows. The other cats may or may not be rats, so 'No cat is a rat' is not certain — II does not follow.

stem:
Statements:
All doctors are graduates.
Some graduates are singers.
Conclusions:
I. Some doctors are singers.
II. Some singers are graduates.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow from the statements?
explanation: The graduates who are singers may or may not include doctors, so I is not certain. 'Some graduates are singers' converts directly to 'Some singers are graduates', so II follows.

stem:
Statements:
No teacher is a doctor.
All doctors are singers.
Conclusions:
I. Some singers are not teachers.
II. No singer is a teacher.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow from the statements?
explanation: All doctors are singers and none of them is a teacher, so the singers who are doctors are not teachers — I follows. Singers who are not doctors may still be teachers, so II does not follow.

stem:
Statements:
Some phones are laptops.
All laptops are tablets.
Conclusions:
I. Some tablets are phones.
II. All tablets being phones is a possibility.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow from the statements?
explanation: The phones that are laptops are also tablets, so some tablets are phones — I follows. Nothing in the statements prevents every tablet from being a phone (laptops inside tablets inside phones fits both statements), so II is possible and follows.
shortcut: A possibility follows if it contradicts no statement

stem:
Statements:
All engineers are graduates.
No graduate is unemployed.
Some unemployed people are artists.
Conclusions:
I. No artist is an engineer.
II. All artists being graduates is a possibility.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow from the statements?
explanation: The unemployed artists are not graduates, but other artists may well be engineers, so I is not certain. Some artists are unemployed and no unemployed person is a graduate, so it is impossible for all artists to be graduates — II does not follow either.
shortcut: Test a possibility against every definite fact

stem:
Statements:
Some boys are players.
Some players are singers.
Conclusions:
I. Some singers are boys.
II. All players are boys.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow from the statements?
explanation: Two 'some' statements give no definite link between boys and singers, so I does not follow. 'Some boys are players' does not mean that every player is a boy, so II does not follow.
shortcut: Some + Some gives no definite conclusion

stem:
Statements: All drives are tests. Some tests are online.
Conclusions:
I. Some drives are online.
II. Some tests are drives.
explanation: "All drives are tests" converts to "Some tests are drives", so II follows. The online tests may or may not include any drives, so I is not certain.
shortcut: All A are B ⇒ Some B are A
